card.name: Citation journal names and 'would be expected'
card.fires_on: Words inside journal citations (Int J, International Journal of) and the word 'be' in 'would be expected to' after a drug class, plus 'effective' after 'not' in drug-interaction text.

modes.label: Journal names in references
modes.description: Abbreviated or full journal title words in a reference list.

modes.label: Would be expected
modes.description: The word 'be' after 'would' when saying other inhibitors or inducers should act similarly.
modes.example: Other inhibitors of CYP3A4 would<< be>> expected to have similar effects.

modes.label: Not effective
modes.description: The word 'effective' after 'not' in interaction statements.
modes.example: Naloxone hydrochloride is not<< effective>> against respiratory depression due to non-opi

card.writes: It suppresses effectiveness and efficacy words, so it steers the next word away from those terms.
card.plain: It fires on journal-title words in references and on 'would be expected' phrasing in interaction sections.
